property_summary: For any inputs to initialize, the contract's public nft getter returns the _nft address passed to initialize; the mutant that sets nft = msg.sender breaks this (for any call where msg.sender != _nft).

For every call to initialize(_baseToken, _nft, ...), the reference stores nft == _nft afterwards; the mutant stores nft == msg.sender, so when msg.sender != _nft the stored nft differs and the property is violated.

After any successful initialize(...) call, the public nft() getter must equal the _nft argument passed; the mutant that delays assigning nft until after setting initialized can allow initialize to succeed while nft() is not the provided _nft for some fuzzed inputs.

After calling initialize(...) the contract's nft() getter must equal the _nft argument whenever initialize returns successfully; the mutant can return successfully while nft() is not set to the provided _nft for some inputs (due to setting initialized = true before nft), so the property is violated for those inputs.

For any inputs, calling initialize(...) either reverts or (if it returns) leaves nft() equal to the _nft argument; the mutant that sets initialized = true before assigning nft can allow initialize to return while nft() is still address(0) when an attacker re-enters initialize (or otherwise observes initialized=true before nft set), so the rule is violated for some inputs when an adversarial callee re-enters during initialize.

For any inputs, calling initialize(...) either reverts or (if it returns) leaves the contract's nft() equal to the provided _nft argument; the mutant (which sets initialized = true before assigning nft) can be broken by a reentrant adversary that observes initialized==true during initialize and causes initialize to return while nft() is not yet set.

For any inputs, calling initialize(...) either reverts or (if it returns) sets the public nft() to the same address passed as the _nft parameter; the mutant that sets initialized = true before assigning nft can be broken by a reentrant NFT receiver that re-enters and causes initialize to complete while nft remains unset.

For any valid initialize(...) call that does not revert, the reference contract sets initialized == true only after completing state updates; the mutant sets initialized true earlier causing initialize to return true while some subsequent state writes could be reverted by reentrant/invalid external interactions — therefore there exists an input (a reentrant or reverting external counterpart) where the mutant leaves initialized == true despite initialize effectively failing to complete updates; the reference never does.

For any inputs to initialize, if initialize completes without reverting then C.initialized() is true; the mutant can set initialized() = true even when a subsequent external call made during initialize reverts, so there exist inputs (an adversarial NFT contract that reverts on safeTransferFrom) where the reference never leaves initialized false when the call fails but the mutant incorrectly leaves initialized true.

For any inputs, calling initialize(...) either completes fully and leaves initialized == true, or it reverts/aborts and leaves initialized == false; the mutant can set initialized = true early and thus may leave initialized == true even when a subsequent external call reverts, violating this invariant.

For any inputs to initialize, the call either completes fully and leaves initialized==true, or it reverts and leaves initialized==false; the mutant that sets initialized=true early can return/leave initialized==true even when a subsequent external interaction reverts, violating this invariant.

For every call to initialize(...), if any external call that occurs after the initialization checks reverts then the reference contract leaves initialized == false (the call as a whole reverts) while the mutant that sets initialized = true early can end up with initialized == true despite the external failure; thus the invariant is that initialize either completes all state updates and sets initialized==true, or it reverts and leaves initialized==false — the mutant violates this when a subsequent external call reverts.
